summary: Three concept directions for one shared household TV home screen, judged and merged into one spec

final.name: Home Team
final.thesis: The den TV's home screen works like a sports broadcast for the whole family: a scorebug clock sits top left, a lower-third marquee names whichever app is focused, and a big Roku-style grid of shows sits beside a standings-style Sports & News board, so a grandparent, a kid or a guest can see every app at once and open any of them in two or three presses.
final.layout:
Canvas 1920x1080. The safe area is x 96-1824 and y 54-1026. Focusable items rest inside a smaller box, x 120-1800 and y 134-1008, so a lifted tile and its ring never cross the safe area. Nothing scrolls. All 16 apps plus Inputs and Settings are on screen at once.

ZONE 1, TOP STRIP, y 54-118 (64 tall). Nothing here is focusable.
- Left, at x 96: the SCOREBUG CLOCK. Three hard-edged blocks, 64 tall, joined with no gaps, square corners, and the last block's right end cut at a 12-degree slant.
  (a) Time block, fixed 220 wide so the layout never shifts between "1:05" and "12:59". Fill #2C271F. "7:42" in Big Shoulders Display 800 at 48px, #F2ECE0. "PM" in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 700 at 26px, #A39A8A.
  (b) Date block, 200 wide, fill #221E18. "Thu Nov 12" in Atkinson 700 at 28px, #F2ECE0.
  (c) Weather block, 160 wide, fill #221E18. A 32px line icon for the condition, then "48°" in Atkinson 700 at 28px. The block is left out entirely when the weather API fails or its data is more than 3 hours old. The slant then moves to the date block.
- Right, right-aligned to x 1824: a 32px microphone glyph, then "Hold mic to ask Alexa" in Atkinson 700 at 26px, #A39A8A. It is plain text with no pill, so it does not look pressable. It is the only place a guest learns how to search.

ZONE 2, MARQUEE (the top area that follows focus), y 134-390, x 96-1824 (1728x256). The panel is not focusable. Only its Continue cards are, when they exist.
- Panel: flat #221E18, square corners. A 16px stripe in the focused app's brand colour runs down its left edge (x 96-112).
- Left zone, x 136-896:
  - Group word at y 158-184, Atkinson 700 at 26px, #A39A8A. It reads "Shows", "Music", "Sports", "News", or "TV" for Inputs and Settings.
  - App name below it in Big Shoulders Display 900 at 112px, #F2ECE0, one line, left-aligned, baseline about y 300. If a name would pass 760px it drops to 96px.
  - At y 320-360: a 40px-tall outlined key cap (2px #A39A8A border, 8px radius) holding "OK" in Atkinson 700 at 24px, then "Open" in Atkinson 700 at 26px, #A39A8A. This is the only instruction on the screen.
- Right zone, default state (always the case when there is no Watch Next data):
  - A parallelogram in the app's brand colour, 600 wide and the full 256 tall (x 1224-1824). Its left edge slants at 12 degrees.
  - On it, the app's own TV banner at 432x243 (the 320x180 banner at 1.35x), y 140-383, right edge at x 1800, with a 2px #14120E keyline.
  - Inputs and Settings show a #2C271F parallelogram with a 120px line icon (HDMI plug or gear) in #F2ECE0 instead of a banner.
- Right zone, Continue state (only when the focused app has real Watch Next items):
  - The brand parallelogram stays.
  - "Continue" label at x 960, y 140-166, Atkinson 700 at 26px, #F2ECE0.
  - Up to 3 cards at 256x144 with 24px gaps, x 960-1776, y 186-330, using the art the app supplied, 2px #14120E keyline.
  - Each card has a one-line title under it at y 338-366 in Atkinson 700 at 24px, ellipsized at the end.
  - If the provider gives a progress value, a 4px bar in the brand colour runs along the card's bottom edge.

ZONE 3, GROUP LABELS, y 414-450. Not focusable.
- "Shows & Music" at x 120 and "Sports & News" at x 1400, in Big Shoulders Display 800 at 36px, title case, #A39A8A.
- Under each, a 4px #3B352B rule at y 446-450 runs the width of its block (x 120-1344 and x 1400-1800) and ends in a 12-degree slant cut.

ZONE 4A, SHOWS & MUSIC GRID, x 120-1344, y 474-1008.
- 4 columns x 3 rows of 16:9 tiles at 288x162 with 24px gaps (4x288 + 3x24 = 1224; 3x162 + 2x24 = 534). Tile corners 6px radius.
- Columns at x 120, 432, 744, 1056. Rows at y 474-636, 660-822, 846-1008.
- Reading order follows how much the household watches:
  - Row 1: Hulu, Peacock, Disney+, HBO Max
  - Row 2: YouTube, Paramount+, Prime Video, Apple TV
  - Row 3: Netflix, Spotify, Inputs, Settings
- App tiles show the app's own banner edge to edge. If an app has no usable banner, the tile shows its brand colour with its name in Atkinson 700 at 36px, bottom-left with a 20px inset (never centred).
- Tiles whose fill is very dark (Peacock, Apple TV, Netflix stand-ins) get a 2px inner border #3B352B so they do not sink into the background.
- Inputs and Settings are utility tiles, styled differently on purpose: #221E18 fill, 2px #3B352B border, a 48px line icon (HDMI plug, gear) top-left with a 20px inset, and the word in Atkinson 700 at 32px bottom-left with a 20px inset.

GUTTER, x 1344-1400 (56 wide). It holds only the possession arrow when a board row is focused.

ZONE 4B, SPORTS & NEWS BOARD, x 1400-1800 (400 wide), y 474-1008.
- 6 standings rows, each 400x78, square corners. These are deliberately not cards.
- CNBC 474-552. Then an 18px gap holding a 2px #3B352B divider at y 562-564. Then ESPN 570-648, FOX One 660-738, NBA 750-828, MLB 840-918, DAZN 930-1008 (12px gaps).
- Each row: a 139x78 chip on the left showing the app's banner scaled to fit (16:9). Then a 261-wide name area, fill #221E18, with the name in Big Shoulders Display 800 caps at 40px, #F2ECE0, left-aligned at +24px.
- If a chip has no banner, it shows the brand colour with the app's icon at 48px.

D-PAD NAVIGATION (set explicitly per item, never guessed from geometry)
- After power-on, or after 4 hours idle, focus starts on Hulu. Pressing Home from inside an app returns here with focus on that app's tile. Back on the home screen always sends focus to Hulu.
- The Shows grid is a plain 4x3 grid with no wrapping.
- Right from column 4: row 1 goes to CNBC, row 2 to FOX One, row 3 to MLB.
- On the board, Up and Down move one row. Left goes to column 4 of the grid row beside it: CNBC and ESPN go to HBO Max, FOX One and NBA go to Apple TV, MLB and DAZN go to Settings.
- Up from grid row 1, or from CNBC, moves into the focused app's Continue cards when they exist. Otherwise it plays the edge bump.
- In the cards, Left and Right move between cards, and Down returns to the tile or row you came from.
- Left from column 1, Right from the board, Down from row 3 or DAZN, and Up with no cards all play the edge bump: the focused item nudges 8px toward the press and springs back, so nobody wonders whether the remote worked.
- Select opens the app. Nothing needs a long press, a menu button or a hidden row.
- Inputs opens a full-screen overlay on #14120E: one row of large 400x225 plates, one per HDMI port, each named with the label the TV reports, using the same focus treatment. Back closes it. If the TV will not report its ports to the launcher, the Inputs tile opens Fire TV's own Inputs screen instead.
- Settings opens Fire TV Settings.

palette.bg: #14120E (warm near-black, like a den at night, never pure black)
palette.surface: #221E18 (marquee panel, board name areas, utility tiles, date and weather blocks); #2C271F scorebug time block and utility parallelogram
palette.text: #F2ECE0 (warm off-white, used for type and icons only; no large pure-white areas anywhere)
palette.muted: #A39A8A (group words and labels, PM, Hold mic line, OK key cap and Open; about 6.9:1 on bg)
palette.accent: #FFB21C stadium-bulb amber, reserved for focus only: the focus ring, the focused board row's name fill and the possession arrow. It appears nowhere else, so amber always means you are here.
palette.extra: #3B352B for rules, the divider, utility borders and inner borders on dark tiles. #14120E for text on amber, art keylines and the 3px gap inside the focus ring. App brand colours appear only in the marquee stripe and parallelogram, board chip fallbacks and stand-in tiles (fill / name colour): Hulu #1CE783 / #14120E; Peacock #0E0E10 / #F2ECE0; Disney+ #113CCF / #F2ECE0; HBO Max #002BE7 / #F2ECE0; YouTube #FF0033 / #F2ECE0; CNBC #005594 / #F2ECE0; Paramount+ #0064FF / #F2ECE0; Prime Video #1A98FF / #0F171E; Apple TV #1C1C1E / #F2ECE0; Netflix #141414 / #E50914; ESPN #D00000 / #F2ECE0; FOX One #0B2A5B / #F2ECE0; NBA #1D428A / #F2ECE0; MLB #041E42 / #F2ECE0; DAZN #F8FC00 / #14120E; Spotify #1ED760 / #14120E. For marquee stripes on near-black brands use a set accent: Peacock #FFC300, Apple TV #A2AAAD, Netflix #E50914, MLB #D50032.

fonts.display: Big Shoulders Display (Google Fonts), weights 800 and 900: clock digits, marquee app name, group labels, Sports & News row names
fonts.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (Google Fonts), weight 700: PM, date, weather, Hold mic line, group word, OK and Open, utility tile words, stand-in tile names, Continue label and titles, Inputs overlay. Nothing on screen is smaller than 24px.
fonts.why: Big Shoulders is a stadium-scoreboard face. Its chunky condensed letters make the clock and the standings board feel like game night, and they fit long names like Paramount+ or Prime Video on one line at 112px. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next was drawn by the Braille Institute for low-vision readers, with letters that cannot be confused (I/l/1, 0/O), so every small word stays readable from the couch for older relatives and kids. Both are under the SIL Open Font License and can be bundled in the app. Neither is on the banned list, and the pair looks nothing like Apple's SF or Roku's type.

final.focus_treatment:
Exactly one item is focused at a time, and it is unmistakable.
- App and utility tiles:
  - Scale 1.10 (288x162 becomes about 317x178), drawn above its neighbours.
  - A 6px amber #FFB21C ring with a 3px #14120E gap between tile and ring. The dark gap keeps the ring readable against Hulu green, Spotify green and DAZN yellow. The ring reaches 23px past the resting tile, which stays inside the safe area.
  - A pre-rendered soft shadow below it (black at 55%, 18px down, 32px soft edge) drawn as a 9-patch, not live blur.
  - The banner art inside the tile starts 4px offset in the direction of the D-pad press and settles to centre over 180ms. It is one translate with no 3D tilt.
  - Unfocused tiles stay at 100% and are never dimmed, so everyone can still read every tile.
- Sports & News rows:
  - The row scales 1.04 around its centre.
  - The 261-wide name area turns solid amber with #14120E text.
  - The same 6px ring with its 3px dark gap wraps the whole row, chip included.
  - A 20x24 solid amber triangle, the possession arrow, appears in the gutter at x 1356-1376, vertically centred on the row and pointing at it, like the highlighted team on a broadcast standings graphic.
- Continue cards and Inputs overlay plates use the same ring and shadow. Cards scale 1.06 from their bottom-centre so they never cover their own title. Plates scale 1.08.
- Select presses the focused item in to 0.96 for 80ms, then the app opens.
- Amber fill or an amber ring never appears on anything that is not focused. The top strip and marquee panel are never focusable.
final.top_area:
The marquee shows only real facts about the focused item.
- Its group word ("Shows", "Music", "Sports", "News" or "TV").
- The app's name, very large, so anyone who cannot make out a small logo still knows where they are.
- Its brand colour, as the left stripe and the slanted parallelogram.
- The app's own TV banner art at 1.35x. For Inputs and Settings, a large line icon.
- The OK = Open key cap.
When an app publishes Watch Next items and the launcher can read them, up to 3 real Continue cards appear on the parallelogram, using that app's own titles, art and progress. With no data, the banner state shows. That empty case is the designed default, not a gap.

The scorebug above shows the real time, date and weather from the API, and drops the weather block when that data is missing or stale.

There are no ads, no rotating carousel, no autoplay, no recommendations made up by the launcher, no scores or prices the launcher does not really have, and no person's name or profile.
final.signature_detail:
The broadcast package runs across the whole screen.
- The time, date and weather sit in a slanted three-block scorebug like the one in the corner of a game.
- Each focus change plays the app name into the marquee like a lower-third graphic.
- The sports and markets apps sit in their own standings board. The focused row lights up amber with a possession arrow, the way a broadcast highlights the team with the ball.
The 12-degree slant on the scorebug, the label rules and the brand parallelogram is the screen's one repeated shape. It keeps the screen from looking like Apple's soft glass or Roku's purple. It reads as game night for the whole household, with nobody's name or data on it.
final.motion:
All motion uses transform, alpha and colour only. It plays only when someone presses a button.
- Focus move: 160ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), scale 1.0 to 1.10. The ring fades in over 100ms and the shadow cross-fades. The parallax settle runs 180ms on the same curve.
- Board rows: the amber fill wipes left to right over 140ms, like a broadcast graphic. The possession arrow slides 8px toward the row as it fades in, also over 140ms.
- Marquee: changes only after focus rests for 120ms, so fast moves do not make it flicker.
  - The brand stripe wipes top to bottom in 180ms.
  - The app name slides in 32px from the left while fading in, over 200ms.
  - The parallelogram slides 24px in from the right over 200ms.
  - The banner art cross-fades in 200ms.
- Held key (repeats under 150ms apart): the marquee waits for the 120ms rest, then swaps with a 120ms cross-fade and skips the slides. This keeps fast movement smooth on a weak GPU.
- Continue cards fade in over 200ms with a 50ms stagger, only after the Watch Next query returns items.
- Select: press to 0.96 for 80ms, then launch.
- Edge bump: an 8px nudge toward the press, back in 120ms with a slight overshoot.
- The clock changes on the minute with no animation, and the colon never blinks. Nothing moves while the remote is idle. Nothing loops and nothing autoplays.
- When the TV's animation scale is set to off, every movement becomes a 120ms cross-fade. Focus scale and ring still apply instantly.
final.feasibility_notes:
BUILD
- A single-activity Android TV app in Kotlin, using plain Views or Compose for TV, not Leanback's browse screen. The layout is fixed and absolute, not a scrolling list. Focus order is set per item with explicit next-focus IDs, exactly as in the D-pad map.
- Rendering is solid fills, text and bitmaps only. There is no video, no live blur and no gradient. The shadow is one pre-rendered 9-patch. The parallelogram is a cached Path. Colour changes use a ValueAnimator.
- About 22 bitmaps on screen (16 banners at about 320x180, one marquee banner, up to 3 cards, a few icons), well under 30 MB. Decode once and keep them in an LruCache. This suits 2.4 GB of RAM and a weak GPU.
- Fonts: Big Shoulders Display and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next bundled as TTFs (SIL Open Font License). No network font loading.

DATA
- Clock and date: system time.
- Weather: Open-Meteo (no key needed), polled every 30 minutes and cached. The town is set once in the launcher's own setup screen. On failure or data older than 3 hours, the weather block is hidden with no dashes or placeholder.
- Banners: PackageManager.getApplicationBanner or getActivityBanner on the LEANBACK_LAUNCHER intent. Launch with getLeanbackLaunchIntentForPackage. Fallback is the brand colour plus the name.
- Brand colours and group membership: a hand-kept table keyed by package name.
- Watch Next: query TvContractCompat.WatchNextPrograms. Reading other apps' rows usually needs a privileged permission that a sideloaded launcher on Fire OS will not get, so the banner state is the real default and Continue is a bonus. Verify on the Den TV before promising it.
- Inputs: try TvInputManager.getTvInputList for the overlay's port names. If Fire OS blocks that or blocks switching, the tile opens Fire TV's own Inputs screen. Check the exact intent on this TV over ADB.
- Settings: android.settings.SETTINGS or Fire OS's settings activity.
- The launcher's own setup (weather town, app order) is a separate app entry kept off the home grid and reached from Fire TV's app list, so kids and guests cannot rearrange the screen by accident.

RISKS TO TEST FIRST ON THE DEN TV
- Fire OS does not let a third-party launcher replace the Home button cleanly. That needs a Home-button intercept (an accessibility service or a launcher-manager setup over ADB), and Amazon updates can undo it. Prototype this before anything else, and keep the stock launcher one press away.
- Alexa voice stays system-level, so search keeps working, but its results open in Amazon's own screens.
- Check ring contrast once real banners are in: amber against Hulu green, Spotify green and DAZN yellow. The 3px dark gap is there for those three.

MOCKUP HONESTY
- Tile art is brand colour plus the app name as a stand-in. The clock, date and weather in the mockup are sample values, not live data. No Continue cards are shown as real.

SCORES (1-10: works for everyone / fits the requester's words / D-pad ease / TV rules / personality / honesty / buildability = total)
- Home Team: 8 / 8 / 8 / 8 / 8 / 9 / 9 = 58. Winner. Everything is visible at once in a chunky grid plus a distinct sports board, so there is no long row. The broadcast theme gives it character that suits a sports-and-markets household. It is the cheapest to build. Weak spots fixed here: focused tiles at the outer edges went past the safe area; board rows did not add up (6x82 plus gaps plus the divider overflowed); amber clock digits muddied "amber means focus"; caps-only group labels.
- Lamplight: 8 / 7 / 9 / 8 / 9 / 9 / 6 = 56. The live-sky window is the most charming idea, but about 20 illustrated landscape sets are real art and asset work. Eighteen identical rounded tiles on shelves lean toward Roku and the "identical cards" trope, and its tiles are the smallest.
- Den Listings: 7 / 9 / 6 / 8 / 8 / 9 / 8 = 55. The magazine cover is the most playful. But Inputs and Settings shrink to small masthead buttons that Up from row 1 can fall into, the right column's rows do not line up with the others, the D-pad map has many special cases, and four section colours on top of 16 brand colours get busy.

WHAT WAS GRAFTED IN
- From Den Listings: the double-rule focus ring (a dark gap inside the amber ring) so it reads on green and yellow tiles; explicit per-item next-focus IDs; the shrink rule for long app names; the held-key rule that skips marquee slides during fast moves; the 0.96 press on Select; the progress bar on Continue cards when the provider gives one; the 2px inner border on very dark tiles; app order edited off the main screen; Open-Meteo with no key.
- From Lamplight: the clearer voice line "Hold mic to ask Alexa"; a fixed-width clock so nothing shifts; focus returning to the app you just left after Home, resetting to Hulu after power-on or 4 hours idle; the full-screen Inputs overlay with big plates named by the TV, with Fire TV's Inputs screen as the fallback; staggered fade-in of Continue cards only after the query returns; stand-in names set bottom-left, not centred.
- Changed from the original Home Team: the layout is reflowed to 288x162 tiles and 400x78 board rows inside a focus-safe box; amber is now used only for focus (the clock digits are off-white); the board row's 12px slide is replaced by a centre scale so the possession arrow fits in a 56px gutter; group labels are title case; utilities show the group word "TV" in the marquee.

Left out on purpose: the illustrated window, the shelf ledges, the Morning/Evening Edition dateline and the section colours. Each is nice alone, but together with the broadcast theme they would muddy it.

concepts.top_area:
The marquee shows only real data about the focused item:
- Its group ("Shows & Music", "Sports" or "News").
- The app's name, very large.
- Its brand colour, as the stripe and the slanted parallelogram.
- The app's own TV banner art at 1.35x.
- An OK = Open hint.
When an app publishes Watch Next items and the launcher can read them, the banner is replaced by up to 3 real Continue cards (title plus the art the app supplied). If no data comes back, that slot simply shows the banner, so the empty case is the designed default rather than a gap.

There are no ads, no rotating carousel, no autoplay, no recommendations the launcher made up and no scores or prices it does not actually have.

The scorebug clock above shows the real time, date and weather from the API, and drops the weather block when that data is missing.
concepts.signature_detail:
The broadcast package, shared across the whole screen.
- The time and date sit in a slanted, three-block scorebug like the one in the corner of a game broadcast.
- Each focus change plays the app name in like a lower-third graphic.
- The sports and markets apps sit in their own standings board. The focused row lights up amber with a possession arrow, the way a broadcast highlights the team with the ball.

It reads as game night for the whole household, with no one person's name or data on it. The slanted 12-degree cuts on the scorebug, the label rules and the brand parallelogram are the screen's one repeated shape, and they keep it from looking like Apple's soft glass or Roku's purple.
concepts.motion:
All motion uses transform and alpha only.
- Focus move: 160ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), scale 1.0 to 1.10. The outline fades in over 100ms. The shadow cross-fades.
- Board rows: the slide left and the amber fill wipe left to right over 140ms, like a broadcast graphic.
- Marquee: changes only after focus rests for 120ms, so fast scrolling doesn't flicker it.
  - The brand stripe wipes top to bottom in 180ms.
  - The app name slides in 32px from the left while fading in, over 200ms.
  - The parallelogram slides 24px from the right over 200ms.
  - The banner art cross-fades in 200ms.
- Edge bump: an 8px nudge toward the press, back in 120ms with a slight overshoot.
- The clock colon never blinks. Nothing moves while the remote is idle.
- If the system's reduce-motion or animation-scale setting is off, every movement becomes a 120ms cross-fade, and focus scale and outline still apply instantly.
concepts.feasibility_notes:
It is built as a lightweight Android TV app (Kotlin, Compose for TV or plain Views).
- Rendering cost:
  - Static layers only, with no video, no live blur and no gradients except the pre-rendered shadow 9-patch.
  - About 22 bitmaps on screen (16 banners at about 320x180 plus a few icons), well under 30 MB of textures, which suits 2.4 GB of RAM and a weak GPU.
- Banner art:
  - Comes from PackageManager.getApplicationBanner, with getApplicationIcon on the brand colour as the fallback.
  - Brand colours and group membership are a hand-kept map keyed by package name.
- Fonts: bundled TTFs, Big Shoulders Display and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, both under the SIL Open Font License.
- Weather: polled from an API every 30 minutes and cached.
- Watch Next is likely unavailable. Reading other apps' Watch Next rows usually needs a privileged or system permission, and Fire OS often keeps its own catalogue. So the banner state is the real default and the Continue state is a bonus if it ever works. Verify this on the Den TV before building it.
- Inputs: opens Fire OS's own input picker by intent. The exact intent and package must be checked on the device; the fallback is TvInputManager or the Settings inputs screen.
- Settings: launches android.settings.SETTINGS, or Fire OS's settings activity.
- Replacing Fire OS's home screen needs an ADB setup or a Home-button intercept app, and Amazon updates can undo it. Plan and test that separately.
- Mockup: tile art is a brand-colour fill plus the app name as a stand-in. The clock, date and weather in the mockup are sample values, not live data.

concepts.name: Lamplight
concepts.thesis: The home screen is a den wall: a picture window at the top shows the real sky outside, and three wooden shelves below hold all 18 tiles at once. The tile you're on lifts off its shelf with a marigold ring, so anyone can see where they are without reading a word.
concepts.layout:
Canvas 1920x1080. Safe frame x 96-1824 (1728 wide), y 54-1026. The background is always dark. Content is left-aligned, nothing is centred, and nothing scrolls: every app is on screen at once.

ZONE 1 - Status strip, y 54-114 (60px tall), full safe width, not focusable.
- Left: clock "7:42" in Bricolage Grotesque 600, 56px, with "PM" at 28px. The clock box is fixed to the width of "12:59" so it never shifts. 20px gap, then the date "Thursday, November 12" in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 500, 28px, muted colour, aligned to the clock baseline.
- Right, right-aligned to x 1824: a 36px line weather glyph, then "52°" in Bricolage 600 36px, then "Cloudy" in Atkinson 28px muted. Then a 32px gap, a 1x32 divider in #3B2E24 and another 32px gap. Then a 30px mic glyph and "Hold mic to ask Alexa" in Atkinson 26px muted. With no search box on screen, this one line is the only way a guest learns how to search, so it stays.

ZONE 2 - The Window (stage), y 134-484 (350px tall), x 96-1824.
- Frame: a 10px walnut frame #3A2A20 with a 1px inner highlight #5A4433 along the top and left edges and a 1px inner shadow #0E0B09 along the bottom and right. Outer corners have a 10px radius and the glass inside has a 4px radius. These square-ish corners keep it from looking like the tiles.
- Glass, about 1708x330: a flat layered landscape. The sky has 2 stops. In front of it are 3 rolling hill silhouettes and 3 to 5 simple trees, all flat fills with no outlines. The set changes with time of day and weather (see palette). Tree colour follows the real season from the date.
- Left info block, inset 56px from the glass edge, sitting on a soft dark scrim (a horizontal gradient from #17120F at 70% to 0% over the first 900px, pre-rendered PNG): the focused app's name in Bricolage Grotesque 700, 88px, colour #F3E9DD, -1% tracking, one line. The longest names ("Paramount+", "Prime Video") are about 560px. The name is vertically centred in the glass at about y 300.
- Sill: a 10px band along the inside bottom edge of the glass in the focused app's brand colour, toned 15% toward #17120F. It repaints when focus moves.
- Watch Next (optional, only if the focused app has published items): up to 2 cards, each 380x214 (16:9) with an 8px radius, at x 1008-1792, top inset 30px. Under each card, 8px down, its title in Atkinson 600 26px, one line with an end ellipsis. The cards sit on a #17120F panel at 80% opacity, 24px padding, 12px radius. With no items the right side is all landscape, which is the expected and designed state on Fire OS.

ZONE 3 - Three shelves, a 6-column x 3-row grid, 18 equal slots.
- Tile 268x151 (16:9, matching the 320x180 Android TV banner), 14px radius, 24px column gap: 6x268 + 5x24 = 1728, edge to edge in the safe area.
- Row 1: y 512-663. Row 2: y 689-840. Row 3: y 866-1017.
- Under each row is a full-width shelf ledge, 1728x8: #3B2E24 with a 1px top highlight #574434. The tiles stand directly on it (ledges at 663, 840, 1017). There is 18px of bare wall between a ledge and the next row.
- Grouping: rows ordered by how much the household watches, so the most-used apps sit closest to where focus starts.
  - Row 1, most-watched shows: Hulu, Peacock, Disney+, HBO Max, YouTube, Paramount+.
  - Row 2, live (sports and markets): CNBC, ESPN, FOX One, NBA, MLB, DAZN.
  - Row 3, the rest: Prime Video, Apple TV, Netflix, Spotify, Inputs, Settings. Inputs and Settings sit bottom-right, where people expect controls.
  - The shelves have no labels. Row 2's ledge is the same wood; the live apps are grouped by position, not decoration.
- App tiles: the app's real TV banner fills the tile edge to edge. Mockup stand-in: a brand-colour fill with the app name in Bricolage 700 34px, set bottom-left with a 20px inset (never centred). Name colour is #FFFFFF or #0B0B0C, whichever has more contrast.
  - Stand-in fills: Hulu #1CE783 (dark text), Peacock #0E0E10, Disney+ #0B1F6B, HBO Max #002BE7, YouTube #282828 (name in #FF0033), Paramount+ #0064FF, CNBC #0A2342, ESPN #C8102E, FOX One #0B0B0C, NBA #1D428A, MLB #041E42, DAZN #0C161C (name in #F7FF1A), Prime Video #1A98FF, Apple TV #1C1C1E, Netflix #141414 (name in #E50914), Spotify #1ED760 (dark text).
- Utility tiles (Inputs, Settings): a dark felt plate #2A211C with a 4% grain PNG and a 1px inner top highlight #3E3128. A 56px line icon (HDMI plug or gear) in #F3E9DD sits top-left with a 22px inset. The label "Inputs" or "Settings" is in Atkinson 600 30px, bottom-left with a 22px inset. Same size and position rules as app tiles, but clearly not an app.

D-pad:
- Focus lands on the tile you last launched. On power-on, or after 4 hours idle, it resets to Hulu (row 1, col 1).
- Left, right, up and down move exactly one slot. Nothing wraps. At an edge, the focused tile does a 6px nudge in that direction and springs back, so the press is acknowledged.
- Up from row 1 goes to the first Watch Next card only if the focused app has cards. Otherwise it is an edge nudge. Left and right move between the cards. Down returns to the tile you came from.
- Select opens the app. Back on this screen sends focus to Hulu. The Home button always returns here, with focus restored.
- Inputs opens a full-screen overlay: one row of large 400x225 plates, one per HDMI port, using the port names the TV reports, plus Back. Settings opens Fire TV Settings.

Window sky sets (top to horizon / hills back to front):
- Morning 05-11: #4E6670 to #B48A64 / #4A5A4E #39463C #2A332C
- Day 11-17: #4F7484 to #7E9AA0 / #5B6B45 #45532F #33402A
- Evening 17-20: #3B2C2A to #B8643A / #3A2A24 #2B2220 #1F1917
- Night 20-05: #101A20 to #1C2A31 / #151C1F #0F1416 #0B0F11, moon #D9CDB8 (44px disc), 12 to 20 star dots #CFC6B4 2px
Weather overlays:

fonts.display: Bricolage Grotesque (Google Fonts, variable, weights 600 and 700, with the opsz axis set high for big sizes): clock, app names on the stage, temperature, mockup tile names
fonts.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (Google Fonts, weights 500 and 600): date, weather word, voice line, utility labels, Watch Next titles, Inputs overlay. Minimum 26px everywhere, 24px only as an absolute floor.
fonts.why: Bricolage has chunky, slightly quirky shapes that feel homemade and friendly without being a novelty face, and it carries the den's character at 56 to 88px. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next was drawn by the Braille Institute for low-vision readers: open counters and letters that can't be confused (I/l/1, 0/O). That suits older relatives reading from the couch 10 feet away, and it pairs cleanly with Bricolage. Neither font is on the banned list, and both are free on Google Fonts and can be bundled in the APK.

concepts.focus_treatment:
Exactly one focused item at any time.
- The focused tile lifts off its shelf: scale 1.08 (268x151 to about 289x163) and translateY -10px.
- Ring: 4px marigold #F2B33D, offset 4px outside the tile. The 4px gap shows the dark wall, so the ring reads on every brand colour, including Hulu green, Spotify green and DAZN yellow.
- Shadow: grows from a resting 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.35) to 0 18px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.55), drawn as a pre-rendered 9-patch, not live blur.
- The segment of shelf ledge directly under the focused tile warms from #3B2E24 to #6B5338, as if a lamp were lit over that spot.
- Every unfocused tile gets a #17120F overlay at 18%. That's enough to make the focused one pop while banners stay readable.
- On Select the tile presses in: scale to 1.03 over 90ms, then the app launches.
- Watch Next cards and Inputs overlay plates use the same ring, lift (scale 1.06) and shadow, so focus looks identical everywhere.
- The window frame and the status strip are never focusable.
concepts.top_area:
The Window, 1728x350. It shows only real things:
1. Time of day and the actual local weather, as a flat illustrated landscape behind glass: sky, hills, trees, plus clouds, rain, snow or fog when the weather service reports them. Tree colour follows the season from the date. Moon and stars show at night.
2. The focused app's name, large, on the left. This confirms where you are for anyone who can't make out a small logo.
3. A sill stripe in the focused app's brand colour.
4. Up to 2 Watch Next cards, only when the focused app has actually published them. Never filler.
The exact temperature and condition sit in the status strip above, next to the clock and date. Fallbacks:
- Weather unavailable: the window shows only the time-of-day sky with no weather shapes, and the strip hides its weather readout entirely, with no dashes or placeholder.
- Inputs focused: the stage reads "Inputs". Settings focused: it reads "Settings".
No ads, no rotating banner, no recommendations, no promos and no personal names.
concepts.signature_detail: The Window. A framed picture window in the den wall that matches the real sky outside: amber in the morning, ember at dusk, moon and stars at night. Snow shows only when it is actually snowing, and the trees turn orange in autumn. Kids notice it, grown-ups read the time and temperature off it, and the focused app's colour paints its sill. Under it, the apps stand on three wooden shelves, so the screen reads as a room rather than a menu. Both effects come from flat vector layers, so the screen has a personality that is neither tvOS gloss nor Roku purple.
concepts.motion:
All motion is short, decelerating and transform-only: scale, translation, opacity and colour, using Android View property animators.
- Focus move: 180ms, curve cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1). The old tile settles back onto its shelf as the new one lifts, with the shadow and ring fading in together. The ledge segment colour changes over the same 180ms.
- Edge nudge: 6px toward the pressed direction and back, 140ms total.
- Select press: scale to 1.03 over 90ms, then launch.
- Stage name: crossfades 160ms with a 6px upward drift on the incoming text.
- Sill colour: tweens 240ms.
- Watch Next cards: fade in at 200ms with a 50ms stagger, only after the provider query returns, and only if items exist.
- Window: changes at most every 15 minutes, with a 1.2s crossfade to the new pre-rendered landscape. Nothing in the window moves continuously: no falling-snow loop, no drifting clouds, no video.
- Home return: tiles fade in from 0 to 100% over 200ms with no stagger. Focus is already on the remembered tile.
- Nothing autoplays, nothing loops and nothing moves while the remote is idle.
concepts.feasibility_notes:
Light on the hardware:
- 18 banner bitmaps decoded at 320x180 (about 4 MB total) and one landscape bitmap of 1708x330 (about 2.3 MB) in memory at a time.
- Landscapes are pre-rendered per sky set and weather (about 4x5 PNG/WebP bundled, or VectorDrawables rasterised once and cached).
- Shadows and scrims are 9-patch or PNG assets, with no RenderEffect blur anywhere. No video.
- This fits comfortably in about 2.4 GB of RAM on a weak GPU.

Data sources:
- Clock: system time.
- Weather: Open-Meteo, which needs no key; the location is set once in the launcher's own settings. Fetch every 30 minutes and hide the readout on failure.
- Banners: PackageManager getApplicationBanner / getLeanbackLaunchIntentForPackage. Some Fire TV apps ship only an icon or a poor banner. The fallback is the stand-in treatment (brand colour plate plus name in Bricolage), which looks intentional because the mockup uses it.

Risks to verify on the actual Den TV before building:
(a) Fire OS limits third-party launchers. The remote's Home button may still open Amazon's home unless it is intercepted with an accessibility-service approach. This is the biggest build risk, so prototype it first.
(b) Reading other apps' Watch Next rows usually needs a system-level permission (READ_EPG_DATA or similar) that a sideloaded app won't get. Treat the Watch Next cards as a bonus that will most likely be empty. The layout is designed empty-first.
(c) Switching HDMI inputs from a third-party app (TvContract passthrough channel URIs) may not be allowed on Fire OS. Fallback: the Inputs tile opens Fire TV's own Inputs screen.
(d) The Alexa button stays system-level, so voice search should keep working on top of the launcher, but results will open in Amazon's UI.

Fonts are bundled as TTFs in the APK, with no network font loading.

concepts.name: Den Listings
concepts.thesis: The home screen is laid out like the cover and listings page of a TV guide: apps are grouped into Shows, Sports, News and Music in uneven magazine columns, and whichever app you land on becomes this issue's cover star, so anyone on the couch can see where they are and what OK will open.

Canvas 1920x1080. Safe area x 96-1824, y 54-1026. Everything focusable sits inside it. Only the cover band's colour runs edge to edge.

1) MASTHEAD, y 54-126 (72px).

Beside it, on the same baseline, a dateline in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 500, 26px, #A8A193: "Thursday, November 12 · Evening Edition". The edition comes from the clock: Morning 5:00-11:59, Afternoon 12:00-16:59, Evening 17:00-21:59, Late Night 22:00-4:59.

3) LISTINGS, y 486-1010.

- Tile rows: r1 y 530-674, r2 y 698-842, r3 y 866-1010.

SHOWS block, x 96-912, 3x3 grid, read left to right in order of how much the household watches each app:
- r1: Hulu, Peacock, Disney+
- r2: HBO Max, YouTube, Paramount+
- r3: Prime Video, Apple TV, Netflix
- Column x positions: 96, 376, 656.

SPORTS block, x 972-1508, 2 columns:
- r1: ESPN as a wide feature tile, 536x144, spanning both columns.
- r2: FOX One (x 972), NBA (x 1252).
- r3: MLB, DAZN.

RIGHT column, x 1568-1824, on its own rhythm (the deliberate asymmetry):
- "News" kicker at y 486-522, then CNBC tile at y 530-674.

- At y 918-1010, a non-focusable voice note: a 32px mic glyph and "Hold mic to search" in Atkinson 500, 26px, #A8A193. Alexa stays the search path and guests learn it here.

Total: 16 app tiles plus 2 masthead buttons. There is no search tile, no ad slot and no rows that scroll. Everything is visible at once and nothing scrolls.

D-PAD MAP (explicit, never guessed by geometry):
- Left/right moves along a row and crosses gutters into the next block on the same row.
  - From Disney+ right goes to ESPN. From ESPN left goes to Disney+.
  - From Paramount+ right goes to FOX One. From Netflix right goes to MLB.
  - From ESPN right goes to CNBC.
  - From NBA right goes to Spotify. From DAZN right goes to Spotify.
  - From Spotify left goes to NBA. From CNBC left goes to ESPN.
  - Left from any column-1 tile and right from the right column do nothing: no wrap, no bounce.
- Up/down moves within a column.
  - Up from FOX One or NBA goes to ESPN. Down from ESPN goes to whichever of FOX One or NBA was last focused (default FOX One).
  - Down from CNBC goes to Spotify. Down from any r3 tile or from Spotify does nothing.
- Up from any r1 tile goes to that app's first Watch Next card if it has one; otherwise to [Inputs]. Up from CNBC goes to [Settings].
- Within the masthead, left/right moves between Inputs and Settings. Down returns to the tile you came from.
- Watch Next cards: left/right between the two cards. Down returns to the app tile that owns them.
- Back on the home screen moves focus to Hulu, the top-left tile. Select launches the app.
- Focus on wake: the last app launched from this screen, or Hulu on cold boot.
- No long-press actions, no hidden menus, no edit mode on the main screen.

fonts.display: Big Shoulders Display (Google Fonts; weights 800 and 900; the variable 'Big Shoulders' family works too)
fonts.why: Big Shoulders is a condensed, heavy, slightly industrial face with real TV-listings and sports-page energy. Because it is condensed, a long name like 'Paramount+' or 'Prime Video' still fits at 150px in the cover headline, and it reads as a magazine cover rather than as Apple's or Roku's system type. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next was designed for low-vision readers: its letterforms are clearly distinct (I/l/1, 0/O), which matters for older relatives reading from 10 feet. Size floor: nothing below 24px. Dateline, buttons and voice note are 26px, kickers 34px, clock 56px, cover headline 150px. Neither face is on the banned list, and the pair avoids the serif-plus-cream trope.

concepts.focus_treatment:
Exactly one item is focused at any time.

The focused tile:
- Scales to 1.08 (256x144 becomes about 276x156) around its centre and moves up 8px.
- Gets a 6px #FFD23F outline set 4px outside the tile, with that 4px gap filled in #12110E. This printed double-rule look stays visible even on the bright green Hulu and Spotify tiles and the yellow DAZN tile.
- Gets a soft drop shadow, 0 18px 32px at 55% black. On device it is a pre-rendered 9-patch, not a live shadow.
- Gets a quick parallax nudge on arrival: the banner art inside the tile starts 6px offset in the direction you pressed and settles to centre, like the art lifting off the card. It uses one translate, no 3D tilt.

Unfocused tiles stay at 100% brightness so the grid never looks dead. Only the focused tile gains the lift, outline and shadow.

Section cue: the kicker of the focused section changes too. Its colour block grows from 14px to 28px wide and its underline goes from 2px to 4px, so you can see you are in Sports without reading anything.

Masthead buttons and Watch Next cards use the same outline. They scale to only 1.05 because they are smaller.

The cover band always names the focused app in giant type, which backs up the outline for anyone unsure what is selected.
concepts.top_area:
The cover band, y 142-462, full bleed. Its background is the focused app's tint colour, with a 6px stripe of the full brand colour along the bottom edge. Content stays inside x 96-1824.

LEFT, x 96 to about 1100:
- y 166-196: the section kicker (a 14x28 colour block, then "Shows", "Sports", "News" or "Music" in Big Shoulders Display 800, 30px).
- The headline: the app's name in Big Shoulders Display 900, 150px, line-height 0.9, #F7F2E8, left-aligned, baseline about y 360. It shrinks to 120px if it would pass 1000px wide.
- y 392-440: an OK key cap (a 2px #A8A193 outlined rounded box, 40px tall, containing "OK" in Atkinson 700, 22px), then "Open" in Atkinson 600, 26px, #A8A193. This is the only instruction on the page, and it tells a first-time user what the big button does.

RIGHT, x 1192-1824, in one of two states.

(a) The app publishes Watch Next items to Android's TV provider:
- Kicker "Continue" at y 166-196.
- Up to 2 cards, 304x171, at x 1192 and 1520, y 206-377. They show the provider's own poster image and nothing else.
- Under each card, at y 389, the program title from the provider in Atkinson 600, 24px, one line, ellipsized.
- Never more than 2 cards, never an invented title. If the item has a progress value from the provider, a 4px bar in the brand colour runs along the card's bottom edge.

(b) No Watch Next data. This is the default, and likely the normal case on Fire OS:
- The app's own banner art at 480x270, centred in the right zone at x 1268-1748, y 167-437.
- It has an 8px #F3EEE4 border and is rotated -2.5 degrees, like a cover photo pasted onto the page.
- When an app has only an icon, the clipping shows the icon at 192px on the brand colour.

No ads, no promoted content, no rotating carousel. The band changes only when you move focus, never on a timer. It shows no ratings, prices or schedules, because a launcher can't get those honestly.
concepts.signature_detail: Every app gets its own cover. When you land on an app, the band fills with its colour, its name appears in huge condensed type like a magazine headline, and its banner is pasted in as a slightly tilted clipping. The masthead nameplate 'Den' carries a dateline that names the edition (Morning, Afternoon, Evening or Late Night Edition) from the clock. Together they make the screen feel like a family TV guide that changes through the day. It is warm, a little playful, built only from real data (the clock, the date and the app's own art), and never shows a person's name or profile.
concepts.motion:
All motion is short, plays only when you press a button, and never loops. There is no idle animation, no autoplay and no ticking.

- Focus move: scale, translate, outline and shadow over 140ms with cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1). The banner's parallax settle runs 180ms on the same curve.
- Cover swap:
  - The band's background colour crossfades over 220ms.
  - The outgoing headline fades out and moves up 16px in 100ms.
  - The incoming headline moves up 24px into place and fades in over 200ms, starting at 60ms.
  - The kicker swaps instantly.
  - The clipping drops in from -6 to -2.5 degrees and from 96% to 100% scale in 240ms with a slight overshoot (spring damping about 0.8).
- Held key: while a D-pad key is held (repeat under 150ms), the cover waits 90ms after the last move before updating and skips the headline slide, swapping it in place. This keeps fast movement smooth on a weak GPU.
- Kicker growth (block width and rule thickness): 160ms.
- Launch: on Select the focused tile does a quick 0.96 press for 80ms, then returns to 1.08, then the app opens.
- Reduced motion: when the system's remove-animations setting is on, every transition becomes a 120ms opacity crossfade, or an instant swap.
- The clock updates on the minute with no animation.
concepts.feasibility_notes:
Build: a single-Activity Android TV app in Kotlin using plain Views or Compose for TV, not Leanback's BrowseFragment. The grid is a fixed absolute layout, not a scrolling list, so focus order can be set explicitly with nextFocusLeft, Right, Up and Down IDs exactly as in the D-pad map. There are no RecyclerView quirks and nothing scrolls.

Rendering:
- The screen is solid fills, text and bitmaps only. There is no blur, video or live gradient.
- Shadows and the focus outline are pre-rendered 9-patches or simple strokes.
- The cover band is one solid-colour View whose colour animates with ValueAnimator (argb). The clipping uses View.rotation, which is cheap.
- 16 banners decoded at 480x270 ARGB_8888 take about 8.3 MB, well inside 2.4 GB of RAM. Decode once and cache in a LruCache.
- Bundle the two fonts as TTF/variable files (about 400 KB total) in res/font.

Data:
- Clock and date: system time. Edition: a time-of-day lookup.
- Weather: Open-Meteo (no key), refreshed every 30 minutes, hidden on failure.
- App banners: PackageManager.getApplicationBanner or getActivityBanner on the LEANBACK_LAUNCHER intent, falling back to the app icon. Launch with getLeanbackLaunchIntentForPackage.
- Brand and accent colours: a hard-coded table for the 16 apps, with androidx Palette extraction for any app not in the table.
- Watch Next: query TvContractCompat.WatchNextPrograms. Reading other apps' rows needs a privileged permission that Fire OS likely won't grant to a sideloaded launcher, so state (b) is the designed default, and state (a) appears only if the query returns rows. Test on the actual TCL Fire TV before promising it.
- Inputs: try the Fire TV input picker intent and fall back to the system Settings inputs screen. The exact intent must be checked on this TV over ADB.
- Settings: android.settings.SETTINGS.

Home button: Fire OS does not let a third-party launcher replace the Home button cleanly. That needs a Home-button intercept (an accessibility service or a launcher-manager approach set up over ADB) and can break after Fire OS updates. Plan for that and keep the stock launcher one press away.

Verify contrast once art is real: yellow outline against Hulu green, Spotify green and DAZN yellow. The dark 4px gap ring is there for those three.

Editing the app list (reordering or adding apps) should live in a separate screen opened from Settings, never on the main grid. That keeps kids and guests from rearranging it by accident.
